The exit-NIM language the stock trades on sits on a rate path the September hike has overtaken, but a 16% drawdown, puts bid and a low observed deposit beta mean most of it is in the price and the bar is disputed, so the lean is small.
A single-analyst bar below Q2 on a bank whose NIM is still expanding, against mortgage and deposit-fee proxies that point the other way; near a non-result.

Management tied the guide to 6.6% mortgage rates and they are 7.4% with applications at a 20-month low, the FY consensus has barely moved, the stock ran 15% into the print and this name's three guide-driven misses in the baseline were -4% to -8.5%; the VantageScore margin story is the one real offset.

Diesel at $6 against a $20-30M H2 freight budget and a guide that needs a +15% Q4 after +1-2% H1 point to a narrowing into a stock that has outrun SPY by 10 points since a beat that was sold; Industrial read-throughs (Fastenal, ISM) are the offset.

Wizards is modelled at +2.5% by the segment bar against a company guide of +MSD and prerelease/UBS evidence of double digits, with a third raise reachable; a 13.5% run-up and +9.8 vol points of put skew keep the lean modest.
The company's own call line items rebuild to EPS 3-4% above a bar barely above Q2, but this name's recent small beats were sold or ignored, so the fact is sized well under the arithmetic.

The '>2.9m subscribers' boilerplate in the date-notice 6-K hints at net adds at or above last year, against an EPS bar that extrapolates the FY guide rather than Q1's +11%; the real earnings reactions (+11, -12, -6, +8) set a large scale and the sign is close to a coin.

Orders +10% and Fastenal +15.5% argue for an organic beat, but Brent averaged $96 in Q3 against $88 when 3M set its $150-175m oil-inflation number, consensus already sits 5c above the guide-implied quarter, and beats without a raise were sold -7% and -2% this year.

Index returns and BlackRock's $135B of iShares inflows cover the ABF line and the EPS bar was trimmed into the print, but fee-rate mix and the expense line that drove -10% in July leave nothing decisive either way.

The July sub-debt redemption saves interest no estimate carries and the bar sits below a clean Q2, against a liability-sensitive CD book meeting the September hike; small net positive on a thin name at 0.94x TBV.

No US hurricane landfall in Q3 and no cat pre-announcement 8-K against a $0.50-0.54 bar that sits $0.30 under three straight $0.83 quarters, with 8.7% of float short; the 9% run-up, soft property pricing and a Q4 Isaias estimate on the call are the offsets.

A first-ever buyback approved five days before the print, inside the blackout, is a board signal a bank with a credit or funding problem would not send; a 99.5% loan-to-deposit ratio and a high-beta deposit base into the hike are the counterweight.
Two Tennessee peers show deposit-cost pressure after SMBK guided NIM to 3.45%, against 15% annualised loan growth; consensus sits on the guide and nothing decides it.

The SYNIT 10-D, which no equity preview reads, shows trust yield falling QoQ for the first time in two years against a guided sequential NIM build, on a name that has sold six of its last eight prints whatever the beat; credit and a likely FY raise are the offsets.

The >$600m FY guide implies a Q4 near $157m after a royalty catch-up Q3 above $186m, and the forward licensing line is what sold the stock -7% in July; against that the price sits below its pre-licence level with backlog +145% YoY, so the scale is large and the sign nearly even.

Steel is 8% above the July 17 futures the guide was pinned to and diesel set a record in the quarter, the same cost line that sold a beat-and-raise -3.9% in July; VMI's beat habit and AZZ's coatings strength offset part of it.

Shorts tripled, puts are bid and the implied move is 2.4x the name's median, so an on-schedule credit print has asymmetric room up; First Horizon's -19% warehouse balances against WAL's 'flat mortgage' baseline are the real negative.

A 2.80% Q4 NIM guide given before the hike on a CD- and FHLB-funded bank, a $25-40M AOCI hit to a stock at 1.45x TBV, and a fee rebuild that lands 2-3% under the bar, against a short book that needs a week to cover.
